titleTag: US Visa Timeline 2026: Application to Passport in Hand
h1: The US Visa Timeline: From DS-160 to Passport in Hand, Stage by Stage
deck: Four stages, and the published wait time measures exactly one of them. Which is why an applicant at a post quoting fifteen days can still be waiting in three months, and why booking flights against an interview date is the most common expensive mistake in this process.
metaDescription: The full US visa timeline in four stages, what each one realistically takes, which one the published wait time measures, and when it is safe to book travel.

headline: The wait time
covers stage two
coverSpec.title: The published US visa wait time measures the interview queue only, which is one of four stages
coverSpec.desc: Stage one is the DS-160 and the application fee, which takes days. Stage two is the interview queue, which ran from about 15 days at Abuja to about 495 days at Toronto in August 2026, and this is the only stage the published wait time measures. Stage three is the interview and the decision, which happens on one day. Stage four is administrative processing where it applies, plus passport return, and it is unpredictable and outside anyone's control.

faq.q: How long does the whole US visa process take?
faq.a: It is dominated by one variable: the interview queue at your post. In August 2026 that ran from about 15 days at Abuja to about 495 days at Toronto. Add a few days for the form and the fee at the start, and an unpredictable stretch afterwards for administrative processing where it applies, plus passport return. At a fast post the whole thing can be a matter of weeks. At a slow one it is well over a year.

faq.q: Does the published wait time include everything?
faq.a: No, and this is the most consequential misunderstanding in this process. The published figure measures how far away the next available interview appointment is, and nothing else. It excludes administrative processing after the interview, which the State Department states explicitly, and it excludes passport return. Two applicants with the same published wait can have completely different total timelines.

There is no reliable answer, and anyone offering one is guessing. It is applied case by case, it can run from days to many months, and there is no meaningful way to influence or expedite it from outside. That unpredictability is the single strongest argument for leaving generous margin between an interview date and any travel you cannot change.

faq.q: When is it safe to book flights?
faq.a: After the visa is physically in your passport, and not before. That is the conservative answer and it is the correct one. Booking against an interview date assumes the interview happens as scheduled, that the decision is immediate and positive, and that no administrative processing follows. Each of those can fail independently, and none of them refunds a ticket.

faq.q: How long does passport return take?
faq.a: It depends on the delivery arrangement at your post and on whether you chose collection or courier. It is usually days rather than weeks once a visa is issued, but it is a real stage rather than an instant one, and it sits after any administrative processing rather than in parallel with it.

faq.q: Which stage can I actually influence?
faq.a: Mostly stage two, the interview queue, and to a lesser extent stage one by not making errors that force you to redo the form. You can influence the queue by booking immediately, checking every post your account offers you, widening the range of dates you will accept, and working the calendar. Stages three and four are not yours to move.

faq.q: Does the MRV fee expire while I wait?
faq.a: It is generally valid for one year from the date of payment, and your interview has to be scheduled within that window. At a post with a queue approaching or exceeding a year, that is not a theoretical concern. If you are holding a distant appointment, check when your receipt was paid, because an expired fee ends your ability to change anything.

cta.heading: Stage two is the only one anybody can help you with
cta.body: That is worth saying on a page about the whole timeline, because it defines what a service like ours can and cannot do. Nobody can shorten administrative processing or speed up a decision. What can be shortened, sometimes substantially, is the wait for the interview itself. If that is the stage costing you the trip, tell us your post, your current date and the widest range you could accept, and we will tell you honestly whether it is worth paying us at all.
